title: Prime perturbations of polynomial observations: instability and incidence criteria
summary: The cost of changing prime signs depends on how the resulting multiplicative function is observed. On a fixed prime support of finite harmonic sum, we prove that existence of a polynomial mean for every sign assignment is equivalent to uniform prime truncation and uniform convergence to local products. The criterion applies separately to ordinary and logarithmic means. For independent activations with finite expected harmonic cost, the almost-sure truncation defect is the averaged large-prime parity probability, not a sum of incidences.
